N-maitre.objects: Banach spaces E1,E2, fixed K and U, and V={K(u)} are all explicit.
N-maitre.domain: Finite T>0, 1<=p<=infinity and some auxiliary 1<r<=infinity are declared.
N-maitre.fixed_and_variable: K and spaces are fixed; u ranges in U and v is exactly its pointwise image.
N-maitre.hypotheses: Compact-set mapping property, U L1 boundedness, measurable V in Lp, uniform Lr bound and uniform target translations are retained.
N-maitre.equations: The two uniform output bounds and the image-set definition are visible in the statement.
N-maitre.quantifiers: Some single r>1 and bounds independent of u/v are used; no relation p=r is imposed.
N-maitre.conclusion: Only V is precompact; p=infinity uses continuous representatives. No convergence of U is promised.
N-maitre.status: Known published theorem; r=infinity follows by restriction to a finite r. No claim of sharpness.
N-maitre.local_definitions: Compact nonlinear map is defined by bounded-set images, so continuity or injectivity is not silently assumed.

scope.evidence_basis: Actual source comparison and author rereading of the fixed node; concrete checks: Reread against published Theorem 2.1 p.1726, not arXiv Theorem 1. K maps bounded sets to relatively compact sets; measurable compositions and Lp membership are explicit, and the auxiliary r>1 differs from p. The r=infinity convention is reduced to any finite exponent on a finite interval. The adjacent prose warns that r>1 is not an optimality claim and that compact images do not recover inputs.
